title: Mary J
content: This is what I saw five days prior to my mother's death, then again two days prior, and again before my mother died. My mom was a very difficult person to be around. She was affectionately known as "Mean Jean" by my sister and me. She was a cruel alcoholic who made my life extremely hard for me. I was terrified of her and completely controlled by her. I honestly don’t recall much kindness from her. I distanced myself from her for two years before she died. In 2007, my dad got sick and passed away on November 15. Mom had been in the hospital with pneumonia and was released for Dad’s funeral. I was afraid to see her because I was in trouble for not visiting her during those two years. She was readmitted to the hospital immediately after the funeral and placed in the ICU, because she was near death herself. I did visit her while she was hospitalized. After a month in a coma, she woke up and began improving. My siblings lived far away, so I knew I would be the sole caregiver. This was a deeply unsettling thought, but I accepted it as my fate. I visited her on December 30, 2007, in room 529. I sat at the end of her bed and talked with her. She was scheduled for physical therapy the following week and would then be released. I truly believed she would do whatever it took to recover enough to go home. On December 31, 2007, I was trying to stay awake until midnight but dozed off; although it didn’t feel like sleeping. I saw my mother in room 529, her head tipped all the way back, with a tube filled with water but the tube wasn’t attached to anything. I watched the water run out of the tube. Somehow, I knew I could call the nurse or let the water run out. I let it run out. The moment the tube was empty, I saw an incredibly bright light under my eyelids. This was like when you close your eyes in sunlight. I wasn’t in the light but looking at it. At the center was an even brighter circle. I knew, without doubt, that God was taking her to heaven. I don’t know how I knew, but I did. I woke up immediately and rushed to check if the hospital had called. They hadn’t called. I waited until morning to call my sister and tell her about this strange dream. Three nights later, I was lying on the couch in my family room while my kids watched TV. This time, I was wide awake but had my eyes closed. The light with the brighter circle appeared again. There were no lights on in the room, just the TV. Two days later, on January 5, 2008, I was getting ready for work at 4:30 AM. The hospital called and told me to come. When I arrived, I entered her room. She was still in room 529. I saw her head tipped back with a tube in her throat. The tube had been disconnected from the breathing machine. I later learned her head was tilted back because they had tried to intubate her. She had passed away. I’ve always wondered why I chose not to save her in the dream and have felt a bit selfish for letting her go. But I believe God was reassuring me she was with him in heaven because I would have always feared the alternative. I’m not psychic. Nothing like this has happened before or since. But I saw my mother’s death and what I believe was heaven’s light. Sometimes, when I wonder if near-death experiences are just the dying brain’s activity, I think of this. My brain wasn’t shutting down, and I saw what I saw. It hasn’t happened since.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Recurrent vision/dream of mother's hospital room (room 529) with disconnected tube draining, followed by seeing a bright light with a brighter circle; later matched circumstances at time of mother's death.
stage_sequence.repeated_stage_detail: The bright light with a brighter central circle appeared on three occasions (5 days prior, 2 days prior, and before death; described specifically on Dec 31 and again three nights later).

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Experience is described as a dream/vision while dozing or with eyes closed (not a personal near-death crisis). Included apparent foreknowledge of mother's death circumstances (disconnected tube) and repeated bright light with brighter central circle interpreted as God taking her to heaven.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I knew, without doubt, that God was taking her to heaven.”
